description: Two analog function generators with a shared logic section, each working as an envelope, an oscillator, a slew limiter or an amplifier; rise and fall times run from 0.5ms to seven minutes

params.text: Sets the rise time of that channel, slower turned clockwise
Sets the curve of that channel's rise, from exponential through linear at the centre to logarithmic
Sets the fall time of that channel, slower turned clockwise
Sets the curve of that channel's fall, from exponential through linear at the centre to logarithmic
Sets the amplitude and polarity of that channel's output, inverting it turned towards POL and passing it turned towards VCA
Adds a voltage between -5V and 5V to that channel's output
Fires that channel's function by hand for as long as the button is held
Sets the timing range of that channel's rise and fall: LOW for very slow modulation, MID for ordinary envelope times, HIGH for snappy percussive ones
Turned on, that channel repeats its cycle with no trigger, which makes it an oscillator
Turned on, that channel holds at its peak while the gate is high and falls once the gate is released; turned off it falls as soon as it reaches the peak

inputs.text: A trigger here starts that channel's rise and fall
The signal into that channel's slew limiter, which smooths and reshapes it
Modulates the rise time of that channel
Modulates the exponential response of that channel's rise and fall times, and with it the frequency of the function
Modulates the fall time of that channel
More than 2V here sets that channel looping, so it repeats its cycle with no trigger
Sets that channel's attenuverter: 0V leaves the amplitude and polarity alone, -5V inverts at full amplitude and 5V passes at full amplitude

outputs.text: Carries a high gate while that channel is rising
That channel's function output, after its attenuverter and its offset
Carries a high gate while that channel is falling
Goes high whenever the X channel is at a higher voltage than the Y channel
The X and Y channels added together
Whichever of the X and Y channels is at the higher voltage
Whichever of the X and Y channels is at the lower voltage

notes: a channel produces nothing until a trigger arrives at its TRIG input, its trigger button is pressed, or its LOOP switch is turned on.
